read: Big pharma is beating and raising. Lilly lifted FY revenue guidance by about $5.5bn at the midpoint, and Merck, Gilead, Sanofi and Regeneron all beat and raised. Healthcare was the best S&P sector on Thursday (+2.4%) while the Nasdaq fell 1.4%, which looks like a rotation into defensive growth. The market is still harsh on companies whose growth isn't speeding up: Alnylam fell 25% despite TTR revenue up 59%, and Iovance fell 36% on data that hadn't improved. Pharma is spending heavily on licensing and acquiring pipeline assets, and the IPO window is still open, with two upsized pricings this week. Immunology and obesity are drawing the money; cell therapy is still out of favour.

items.headline: Lilly Q3: revenue +39% to $24.4bn, and FY revenue guidance raised to $91-92bn (from $85-87bn)
items.detail: Mounjaro $10.7bn, Zepbound $5.4bn, Foundayo (orforglipron) $184m. Non-GAAP EPS guidance trimmed to $35-36 on a $4.57/sh acquired pipeline charge (AtaiBeckley, Merida). Stock +6.6%.

items.headline: Regeneron Q3: revenue +36% to $5.1bn; Sanofi pays $1bn upfront, up to $7bn more in milestones, for next-generation long-acting immunology antibodies
items.detail: EYLEA HD US sales +62% while EYLEA US fell 41%. FDA decision on cemdisiran (gMG) due in November.

items.headline: Alnylam -25%: TTR guidance held at $4.2-4.5bn, but management expects the low end and no Q4 acceleration
items.detail: TRITON-CM grows by 500 patients. The $2.2bn GAAP profit includes a one-off tax benefit of about $1.9bn.

items.headline: Iovance -36%: updated IOV-LUN-202 lung cancer response rate 24.6% (17/69)
items.detail: A biomarker subgroup showing 59% was picked out after the fact, not pre-specified.

items.headline: Sanofi Q3: sales +14.3% at constant currency to EUR 14.4bn, and FY guidance upgraded
AstraZeneca Q3: revenue +7% at constant currency, core EPS +19%, FY guidance reconfirmed
IPOs: Bambusa raises $168.9m at $16, upsized; Aspen Neuroscience raises about $141m
